subject: UniProtKB:P36561
description: This gene-product/activity edge retains the reviewed K-12 assignment without asserting a physical monomer catalyst. The 2021 construct is BL21-derived; the 2023 work separately supports engineered MG1655 CobS function. Cyanation during product analysis limits inference about the native upper ligand from the final peak. The 2023 supplement misnames the product as adenosylcobinamide-5-P; the independently balanced Rhea equation is retained. No direct E. coli cobamide-remodeling activity is assigned.

subject: SGD:S000000227
description: Physical protein location from reviewed UniProt. ECO:0000269 (PubMed:12928491); ECO:0000269 (PubMed:17519287); ECO:0000269 (PubMed:28346351) Topology: Multi-pass membrane protein. Source qualification: Localizes to a ring on the surface of cells about to undergo bud emergence and in the mother-bud neck of small-budded cells (PubMed:8909536). description: UniProtKB reviewed (Swiss-Prot) annotation. UniProt evidence: ECO:0000255 (HAMAP-Rule:MF_00388); ECO:0000269 (PubMed:10026271); ECO:0000269 (PubMed:20709752) Can use either Fe(2+) or Zn(2+). The metal cofactor can switch between Fe(2+) and Zn(2+) in response to metal availability. Metal switching may be important for regulating the LpxC activity upon changes in environmental conditions. Has a significantly higher affinity for Zn(2+), but exhibits higher activity with Fe(2+) (PubMed:20136146, PubMed:20709752). Can also use Co(2+), Ni(2+) and, to a lesser extent, Mn(2+) (PubMed:10026271). UniProt note evidence: ECO:0000269 (PubMed:10026271); ECO:0000269 (PubMed:20136146); ECO:0000269 (PubMed:20709752)

subject: UniProtKB:P54745
description: MngA is one 658-residue EIIABC chain. MC4100 mngA deletion loses MG transport and pACS31 restores it; inverted membranes plus general PTS extracts and PEP form MG-P. This is not a purified three-protein reconstitution. Separate intact-cell uptake comparisons in MG-induced MC4100 reported weak reduction with glucose, mannose and mannitol, a smaller effect with trehalose, and no observed reduction with fructose, maltose, arabinose, gluconate, glycerate, 1-alpha-glucosylglycerol, 2-alpha-glucosylglycerate or 2-alpha-mannosylglycerol. The Discussion instead describes mannose and those three glycosyl analogues as not significantly inhibitory even at 1 mM against 0.1 micromolar radiolabeled MG; the mannose weak-effect/no-significant-effect tension remains unresolved. These are uptake comparisons, not direct binding, a proven competitive mechanism or inhibition constants. Separately, 300 mM NaCl during growth did not induce transport and reduced MG-dependent induction by about 50%; this is an induction endpoint, distinct from the KM522 500 mM salt-protection experiment and from a direct catalytic salt effect. None of these whole-cell comparisons is attributed to the pACS31 inverted-membrane assay.

subject: SGD:S000002403

Omitted products and balancing species remain unresolved, rather than asserted absent.
